svg.text: The schism in one picture: who should lead after Muhammad?
Teach this left to right. The split is about succession. It is not a split over whether there is one God.
632: Muhammad dies in Medina
Arabia is united. No successor both sides accept.
Sunni path: the community chooses
632: companions at Saqifa elect Abu Bakr, the first caliph.
Sunna = the way of Muhammad. Leader should be a qualified Muslim.
The first four caliphs are later called the Rashidun, rightly guided.
Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman, then Ali.
Shia path: leadership stays in the family
Shia from shiatu Ali, partisans of Ali.
Ali: cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad. Married to Fatima.
Claim: the rightful leader must come through Muhammad's bloodline.
Ali is the first Imam. His descendants are the Imams.
What happened next: say these three dates
656: Ali becomes the fourth caliph. He rules from Kufa. He is killed in 661.
661: Muawiya begins the Umayyad caliphate at Damascus. Shias do not accept this dynasty.
680: Karbala, in Iraq. Soldiers of Yazid, the second Umayyad caliph, kill Ali's son Husayn.
Later, Shias themselves split over which descendant was the next Imam
Zaydi: split at the 5th Imam
Mostly in Yemen.
Imam rule there lasted into the 1960s.
Smallest of the three branches.
Ismaili: split at the 7th Imam
Important in South Asia, and in a diaspora.
Nizari Ismailis revere the Aga Khan as the
living representative of their Imam.
The Fatimids of Egypt were Ismaili.
Twelver: twelve Imams
Majority of Shias. Iran, Iraq, and others.
12th Imam entered occultation, hiddenness,
around 941. He will return at the end of time.
Senior scholars are called ayatollahs.
Sunni imam usually means the person who leads prayer. Shia Imam means the rightful leader from Ali's line. Do not mix the two.
Classroom guide, not a full family tree. Dates follow the standard exam account. Source: CFR, The Sunni-Shia Divide.
